name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Thermal Longsword TL-3 'Cauterizer'
description:
A longsword-profile weapon with a blade that incorporates a resistive heating element running the full length of its cutting edge, raising the blade temperature to 1,400 degrees Celsius within three seconds of activation. The Cauterizer does not merely cut — it melts through materials that a conventional blade could never penetrate, leaving cauterized wounds that seal as they open and slag-edged cuts through metal and composite barriers.

The blade itself is constructed from a tungsten-ceramic composite that withstands its own operating temperature without deformation. A thermal insulation layer separates the heated edge from the blade's spine, allowing the weapon to be wielded without protective gloves — though the radiant heat from the active edge is uncomfortable at close proximity and can cause minor burns to exposed skin within 30 centimeters. The handle contains a compact fuel cell that provides approximately 90 minutes of continuous heating.

Arcturus designed the Cauterizer for breaching operations where powered cutting tools are too bulky and explosives too dangerous. The weapon can cut through reinforced doors, security barriers, and light vehicle armor given 10-15 seconds of sustained contact. Its adoption as a combat weapon was driven by field operatives who discovered that the psychological impact of a glowing blade was as tactically valuable as its cutting capability.

weight: 2.1 kg
edge_temperature: 1,400°C operational
heat_time: 3 seconds to operational temperature

blade_material: Tungsten-ceramic composite
thermal_insulation: Aerogel-reinforced spine barrier
tactical_use: The Cauterizer serves dual roles as a breaching tool and close-combat weapon. Breaching teams use it to cut through barriers silently when explosive charges would alert defenders or risk structural damage. In combat, the weapon's thermal edge defeats any personal armor by melting through it rather than relying on kinetic force. The radiant heat creates a 30cm danger zone around the active blade, discouraging grappling and close-in defense. The visible glow of the heated edge in dim environments makes the wielder a conspicuous target, requiring tactical awareness about when to activate.
cultural_context: The glowing blade of an active Cauterizer has become one of GLMZ's most recognizable visual threats. Security footage of thermal longsword breaches has circulated widely enough that the image carries immediate cultural meaning: someone with a Cauterizer is not negotiating. The weapon has also developed a grim reputation in GLMZ's medical community — cauterized wounds are notoriously difficult to treat, as the thermal damage extends deep into surrounding tissue and resists standard surgical repair.
story_hooks: A series of vault breaches used Cauterizers to cut through walls rather than doors — bypassing all security on the entry points. The thieves left the slag-edged cuts as calling cards.

A Cauterizer has been recovered with its thermal limiter removed — the edge temperature exceeded 2,000°C and partially melted the blade's own structure. Someone is pushing the weapon beyond its design limits for a specific target.

physical_description.visual_profile: A longsword-proportioned weapon with an aggressive, functional aesthetic. The blade tapers to a sharp point with a subtle fuller running its length. When inactive, it appears as a dark, utilitarian melee weapon with industrial overtones. When active, the cutting edge glows brilliant orange-white, creating an unsettling halo effect that radiates visible heat shimmer into the air around it.
physical_description.dimensions: Blade length 85 cm, total length 118 cm, blade width approximately 5 cm at the widest point near the crossguard
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced — 2.1 kg distributed evenly along the blade and handle, making it feel substantial in hand without being unwieldy. The weight favors the blade slightly, giving momentum to cuts.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten-ceramic composite blade with a steel or titanium alloy spine and crossguard. Handle is reinforced polymer or anodized aluminum with integrated fuel cell housing.
physical_description.finish: Blade has a dark gunmetal matte finish with faint striations where the thermal insulation layer meets the cutting edge. The spine shows brushed metal treatment. Handle features a textured non-slip polymer coating, slightly weathered from field use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray and dark gunmetal primary; glowing orange-white cutting edge when active. Accent details in anodized blue or red (manufacturer color-coding visible on crossguard and pommel cap).
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured thermoplastic polymer with embedded grip channels, slightly rubberized to prevent slipping when sweat or moisture is present. Warm to the touch even when inactive due to residual heat from the fuel cell.
distinctive_features: Visible thermal insulation layer as a darker band running parallel to the cutting edge
Small LED indicator near the crossguard showing fuel cell status (green/yellow/red)
Venting slots along the blade spine for heat dissipation
Crossguard with angled, aggressive geometry — designed to catch and bind opponent weapons while the heated edge remains exposed
Pommel cap with fuel cell access panel and recessed status display
Fine hairline cracks or discoloration in the blade finish from repeated thermal cycling
Subtle scoring marks along the blade from previous breaching operations
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (stylized 'Φ' symbol merged with a thermal wave motif) stamped into the crossguard. Serial number etched along the blade's spine near the hilt. Restricted weapon classification mark (red triangle with thermal warning symbol) visible on the pommel cap.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but showing field wear — minor surface scoring, faint heat discoloration near the tip, grip slightly worn in high-contact areas. Fuel cell housing shows signs of regular maintenance access. Overall condition suggests professional use by trained operatives rather than street-level combat.
